strings.contentAiNote: An AI model, {model}, named the groups from the titles of their articles. The names are an experiment: no editor has checked them, and they can be wrong.
strings.contentAiNoteShort: The group names were generated by AI.
strings.contentExcluded: Not shown: {furniture} notices and lists (contributors, books received, back matter), {short} very short texts, and {shared} items with no text of their own.
strings.contentGroupsOverTimeAria: Grid of the groups of similar articles against the decades, shaded by each group’s share of the decade.
strings.contentGroupsOverTimeNote: How many of each decade’s articles fall in each group. The shade shows the group’s share of the decade, so a decade with few articles reads as clearly as a busy one.
strings.contentIntro: Each dot is an article, placed by the words of its full text rather than by its title or keywords. Articles that discuss similar things sit close together, whatever their decade. Only the distance between dots matters: the axes have no meaning, and the groups are found by the computer, not chosen by an editor.
strings.contentMapAria: Map of the articles by the content of their full text. Articles about similar things appear close to each other.
strings.contentMethod: How it is made: each article’s full text is cut into passages of about 300 words, and the open embedding model {model} turns each passage into a semantic embedding, a list of 768 numbers that captures what the passage is about. An article’s embedding is the average of its passages’. UMAP projects the embeddings onto the map, HDBSCAN finds the groups, and an article’s closest articles are those whose embeddings are most similar (cosine similarity). The full text itself stays private: the page receives only the positions and the lists of closest articles.
strings.contentNoNeighbours: No other article on the map is close to this one.
strings.contentNoSearchResults: No article on the map matches that search.
strings.contentPlacesArticlesDecade: Articles of the {decade}s that write about {country}
strings.contentPlacesHint: Select a country on the map, or in the table under it, to list the articles that write about it.
strings.contentPlacesIntro: The countries the articles write about: the darker a country, the more articles name it. Choose a decade to see how the journal’s attention moved, and select a country to list its articles.
strings.contentPlacesList: Countries and their number of articles
strings.contentPlacesMethod: An article counts for a country when its full text names it at least {min} times, by its present name, a colonial name (Gold Coast, Nyasaland, Belgian Congo…), its adjective, or a few regions and cities such as Buganda or Zanzibar. The journal’s own addresses are left out, and a bare “Congo” counts for the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Africa and the African Americas only. Found by matching names, so expect a few mistakes; the texts themselves stay private.
strings.contentPlacesNoArticles: No article of this decade writes about it.
strings.contentRecordList: List of the articles on the map, by group
strings.contentSearch: Find an article on the map
strings.contentSelectHint: Select an article on the map, or find it by its title, to list the articles closest to it in content.
strings.contentWordsAria: Line chart of how often these words occur per 10,000 words, by year: {words}.
strings.contentWordsFull: Six words at most: remove one to add another.
strings.contentWordsIntro: How often words occur in the articles of each year, per 10,000 words. Compare up to six: type a word and press Enter, or add one of the frequent words.
strings.contentWordsMethod: Counted in the full texts of the {articles} articles on the map, from {first} to {last}. Only words found in at least {min} articles are counted, and the texts themselves stay private: the page receives only the counts. Years with few articles swing widely; the {years}-year average evens them out.
strings.contentWordsMissing: Not counted: {words}. A word is counted only when it occurs in at least {min} articles.
